_comment: Issue years for works published serially in numbered plates, where the catalogue would otherwise carry one blanket year for the whole set. Applied by build-data.mjs AFTER metadata/date-overrides.json, so a researched per-work correction still wins over a band. The plate number is read from the leading digits of the filename (e.g. '318_American_Avocet.jpg'). A work whose plate number falls outside every range keeps whatever the normal extractors gave it. Regenerate data with 'pnpm assets:build-data' after editing.

audubon-birds._why: All 435 Havell plates shipped dated 1827 because their date_created reads 'between 1827 and 1838' and resolveYear collapses a stated range to its opening year. Only plates 1-30 were defensibly 1827; the rest were wrong by a median of 6 years and up to 11, which put a seventh of the corpus on one false point in the timeline. The bands below are Boston Public Library's per-plate engraved-imprint dateIssued values (547 records re-harvested; 379 carry a single-year imprint, 374 of which match their band), cross-checked against the Metropolitan Museum collection API on 8 plates spread across the range and the Smithsonian on 4 more, with zero unexplained conflicts. Every band boundary falls on a Havell Number boundary and the implied sets per year sum to exactly 87.
audubon-birds._caveats: These are engraved-imprint years catalogued as dateIssued, not certified issue dates: a very good approximation of a serial publication event, not a signed inscription. Two bands are marked confidence 'inferred' rather than 'imprint': no plate anywhere in the set carries an 1827 imprint, so plates 1-30 rest on publication demonstrably beginning in 1827, plate 31 being imprinted 1828, and the Met independently dating plate VIII and the plate XI copperplate to 1827; and only 9 of the 30 plates in the 1831 band carry an 1831 imprint, though its edges are pinned by 1830 ending at 100 and 1832 beginning at 131. Plates 2 and 7 are imprinted 1829 because Lizars began the first ten and Havell re-engraved them, and 287/289/290 are imprinted 1835 while their setmates 286 and 288 are imprinted 1836; both groups are dated by ISSUE rather than by impression state, which is the correct choice for a subscription serial. Plate 55 is the one known soft spot (NMAH dates an impression 1835 against BPL's 1829 imprint). Commons is useless here: its file pages carry the same 'between 1827 and 1838' that caused the problem. If certified issue dates ever surface they should override this.
